extracted.intended_audience: NIH F31 predoctoral fellowship applicants, sponsors/mentors, and NIH peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and summary statement for an NIH F31 predoctoral fellowship application, covering criteria such as applicant quality, mentorship, research training plan, institutional environment, and required compliance elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact/Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact/Merit: the reviewers' overall level of enthusiasm for the application and likely impact of the proposed work on the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers summarize significance, novelty, feasibility, preliminary data, quality of training plan and mentor match. Example text: "This is a timely and important topic... likely to have significant overall impact..." and "in spite of some minor concerns, I have a high level of enthusiasm for this application." Overall impact is reflected in the averaged overall scores of voting reviewers (see scoring process).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the applicant's qualifications, academic record, prior achievements, commitment to research, and potential for becoming an independent investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers cite degrees, scholarships, advocacy roles, recommendation letters, course performance, research productivity, and background (e.g., "first in his family to attend college"). Strengths/weaknesses are enumerated (e.g., strong supportive letters; occasional note of moderate undergraduate performance). Numeric criterion scores (1-9) are used by reviewers when rating this dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsors, Collaborators, and Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the primary sponsor/mentor and other collaborators: qualifications, track record in mentoring, availability of support, and fit with the applicant's training needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider sponsor's publication and mentoring record, funded research, history of trainees placed in faculty positions, and evidence of sufficient time to mentor (e.g., "sponsor will be training one doctoral student, 2 postdoctoral trainees"). Strengths often include well-established, well-funded mentors; weaknesses are noted if mentoring resources are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality, feasibility, appropriateness, and novelty of the proposed research and how it serves as a vehicle for the applicant's training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for solid rationale, strong preliminary data, feasible experimental plans, alternatives and expected outcomes described for each aim, appropriate techniques and available expertise, and explicit training goals tied to research tasks. Example strengths: "experimental plan is highly feasible," "expected outcomes and alternatives for each aim are well described." Example weakness: use of a non-natural infection route (ip) noted as a minor concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Likelihood that the proposed training and environment will develop the applicant's skills and advance their path toward research independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider availability of seminars, workshops, professional development, specific course attendance (e.g., NIA Advanced Course on the Biology of Aging), frequency of meetings, mentor-mentee relationship quality, and explicit plans to acquire new technical skills. Strengths include clearly described opportunities and tailored training; weaknesses include lack of plans to acquire cutting-edge techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Environment & Commitment to Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the institution's facilities, resources, and commitment to the applicant's training and career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess quality of facilities, institutional support, interactions with other faculty/students, and explicit evidence of institutional commitment. Typical judgments: "environment and institutional support is excellent."

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals (Animal Subjects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the use of vertebrate animals, including whether animal-related points are addressed and whether procedures/numbers are appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: "YES, all five points addressed." Reviewers check appropriateness of species, numbers, procedures for immunization and infections, and overall animal welfare considerations. Committee verdicts use labels such as "ACCEPTABLE" or specify concerns; here: "The use of mice, numbers of animals, and procedures ... are appropriate." Also shows Animal Subjects summary line: "Animal Subjects: 30-Vertebrate animals involved - no SRG concerns noted."

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of biosafety and biohazard issues associated with the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review includes agent risk level (e.g., "Mouse CMV is a BSL2 agent"), sponsor/team experience with agent, and whether there are biosafety concerns. Verdicts recorded as "Acceptable" when no concerns are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the proposed RCR training component for the trainee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required comments address format, subject matter, faculty participation, duration, and frequency. Example specifics given: "9 hours of RCR instruction, comprised primarily of live workshops...", "Contains the NIH-required topics.", "Nine-week course session", "Every week over the course of a semester.", and "Faculty participation is noted." Reviewers rate the RCR plan (e.g., "Acceptable").

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to share data, resources, and other materials resulting from the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers mark the adequacy of resource sharing plans; in this case the plan is labeled "Acceptable." No further detail provided in the summary, but adequacy is considered part of review/compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of requested budget and period of support for appropriateness and reasonableness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee provides budget recommendations (e.g., "Recommend as Requested"). Budget justification and period are reviewed for fit with the proposed work and training plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the project involves human subjects and any human subjects protections required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary line records status (here: "Human Subjects: 10-No human subjects involved"). If human subjects are involved, reviewers evaluate protections and associated concerns; if none, reviewers note absence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement of the project's relevance to public health and broader impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant-provided public health relevance is assessed for significance; example: linkage of CMV infection to metabolic health decline (glucose intolerance, insulin resistance) and potential implications for vaccinology, immunology, virology, and endocrinology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Scoring Process / Impact Score Calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural description of how scores are collected and how the overall impact/priority score is calculated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion scores (1-9) are submitted prior to the meeting by assigned reviewers and are not discussed at the meeting; the impact/priority score is calculated after discussion by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking. See NIH peer review process for details.
